Tag checks spring basics
Every shift teaches something

Companion Animal Travel Desk page: spring basics and why they matter. New staff need this because animal travel runs on calm checks, clear notes, and steady handoffs between the desk and the cabin team. When the file is clean, the trip feels smoother for everyone, including the traveler and the pet.

Start with the booking record and read every service note before you speak to the customer. Keep your tone plain and helpful. If the animal is accepted for travel, make sure the details match the approved service and the bag, crate, or carrier description. The cabin team watches for comfort, water, and safe placement, so the desk must send clean information without guesswork. <<FACT F078>> Do not leave gaps in the ledger, because small misses turn into messy fixes later.

For smaller pets, the fee note must be checked before payment is taken. <<FACT F056>> If the traveler asks about extras, stay with the written record and route anything unusual to the senior coordinator. Never promise what you have not verified. Every note should show the animal type, the service path, and any change made after the first booking. If a traveler arrives flustered, slow the pace and read back the key points in simple words.

Remember that the desk is not just paperwork. It is part of the animal's care chain, and the next handoff depends on what you write today. Keep the record tidy, the language clear, and the service steady. What to remember: clean notes, calm voice, and careful checks keep the journey on track.
